question: Should the final judge of a ceremony be a deterministic policy engine or an LLM-as-judge? Decide: accept (deterministic policy), reject (LLM-as-judge), request_changes or request_more_evidence.

evidence.text: Run csi-typha-1 (real): the LLM judge ruled with confidence 'High' explicitly citing evidence that another agent had fabricated ('privileged:true in the pod spec' — absent from the case file). The LLM judge did not detect the fabrication.

Run csi-typha-appeal-1 (real): when confronted with its earlier failure, the LLM judge lowered its confidence to 'Medium' and vacated the original verdict — LLM judges can improve with better context, but calibration arrived only after the damage.

The engine ships a deterministic rejection path: OutputContract validation in the deliberation pipeline ends in NoValidProposal{contract_id} with production validators (verified e2e in PR #118's test where prose-only proposals die against a ruling-contract).
The LLM judge consumes provider tokens on every deliberation (judge model invocations recorded in engine metrics); a policy gate evaluates schema and evidence refs without any model call.
The engine's judge selects winners by intrinsic quality instead of arbitrary tie-break (CHOREO_JUDGE_ENABLED); a pure policy gate cannot rank two proposals that both satisfy the contract.
